title: Part Thirty-Three: The Inquisitions Beyond Rome

sections.brief: Spanish Inquisition 1478 (Exigit sincerae, crown-named Suprema, Sixtus IV's 1482 protest), conversos and the Alhambra Decree 1492, Moriscos and the 1609 expulsion, Cisneros's 1499 Granada book-burning, Protestants 1558-62, alumbrados, Spanish indexes; death-toll estimates by named historian (Llorente to Contreras-Henningsen, Kamen, Monter, Pérez, Ereticopedia) and Borromeo 2004; Portugal 1496-97 forced baptism, Cum ad nihil magis 1536, Almeida/Lea counts, abolished 1821; Rome: Licet ab initio 1542, Del Col's estimate, Holy Office 1908, CDF 1965, DDF 2022; Spanish abolitions 1808-1834 and Ripoll 1826. Figures: compare (estimates), time

Crown orders against temples 1541 and 1546, temple counts (Goa island, Bardez, Salcete; 1569 letter), Mangueshi linga moved 1560; Xavier's letter (1545/46, disputed meaning); tribunal 1560, New Christians then Hindu converts (Saraiva, Lehner); 1567 laws, Konkani ban 1684/1687; records burned; Benton, Saraiva counts (57 burned, 64 in effigy); suspension 1774-78, abolition 1812; Synod of Diamper 1599 and Syriac books; Priolkar vs Tavares/Menezes historiography; Sawant 2021. Figures: stats

Don Carlos Ometochtzin 1539 and the Indigenous exemption (1571); tribunals Lima 1570, Mexico 1571, Cartagena 1610 and their targets; Landa and Maní 1562 (6,300 questioned, 157 dead, 27 codices; Toral; Relación and Knorozov); four Maya codices, Maya Codex of Mexico 2018; Zumárraga charge graded (Icazbalceta); Itzcoatl's burning; Sahagún's Florentine Codex and Philip II's 1577 confiscation; Third Council of Lima on quipus; extirpation of idolatries 1609-1670 (Ávila, Arriaga 1621, Villagómez; Mills, Griffiths); labelled interpretation on inner knowledge. Figures: compare (tribunals vs bishops)
